forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Salford housing service forecasts £3.6m overspend and cannot meet £1m savings target after mid-year transfer
news_drafts.lead: Salford's housing service, transferred to the Place Directorate mid-year, is forecasting a £3.6m overspend driven by housing benefit subsidy losses and demand pressures in supported housing and housing options. The service cannot deliver its budgeted £1m savings target. In a statement to the scrutiny panel, the council said the service is "not yet sufficiently embedded within the directorate to identify, develop and deliver sustainable savings of this scale without risking service performance" and will need to develop a fresh plan once new leadership arrangements are in place. After drawing £1.76m from reserves, the net overspend stands at £1.8m. The housing capital programme has also been reproffiled down by £17m as contract arrangements are finalised, with the council acknowledging risks to future delivery from staffing and third-party dependencies.
news_drafts.paper_title: Report - Q1 - Place Directorate budget report - LMB HAP

news_drafts.headline: Salford misses accounts deadline for second year as auditors plan third disclaimer of opinion
news_drafts.lead: Salford City Council has failed to publish its draft accounts for 2025/26, missing the 30 June statutory deadline by nearly three months. The council faced the same delay last year, when accounts were published on 25 September due to problems valuing its property, plant and equipment (long-lived assets such as buildings). Auditors plan to issue a disclaimer of opinion for the third consecutive year, meaning they will not have completed enough work to confirm the accounts are correct. The council's auditors have identified a new risk of significant weakness in how it manages statutory financial reporting. The council is transitioning to a new financial system during 2026/27, and auditors have engaged specialists to verify that data transfers correctly before the next audit begins.
news_drafts.paper_title: Salford City Council Audit Progress Report Sept 2026

news_drafts.headline: Salford's cash reserves fall 32% as council relies more on internal borrowing
news_drafts.lead:
Salford's available investment balances fell from £106.2m to £72.7m in the year to March 2026, a decline of nearly a third, while the council simultaneously increased its internal borrowing (using its own reserves to fund capital projects rather than taking loans) from £224.7m to £256.6m. The council attributes higher-than-forecast cash balances to slippage in its capital programme, with actual capital spending reaching only £103.9m against a forecast of £113.6m. The combination means the council is drawing down its liquidity cushion while depending more on its reserves to bridge the gap between planned spending and external borrowing. The council also holds £163m in LOBO loans, representing 59 per cent of its total external debt. During 2025-26, one lender exercised its option to propose a higher interest rate; the council declined multiple prepayment offers.

findings.paper_title: Report - Q1 - Place Directorate budget report - LMB HAP
findings.headline: Housing capital programme reprofs £16.95m with acknowledged risks to future programme delivery from staffing
findings.detail: Housing Strategy and Enabling capital programme reduced by £16.950m following review, reflecting 'revised cashflow forecasts while main contract arrangements are finalised.' The paper acknowledges broader capital programme risk: 'further likelihood of re-profiles... due to the scale, complexity, fluidity, and broad aspect of the portfolio' with specific risks from 'staff retention and recruitment, as well as interdependencies on third parties.'
findings.matters: Major capital reprofiling and acknowledged risks to delivery signal either slippage or reprioritisation of significant investment, with staffing constraints limiting delivery capacity.
findings.figures: £16.950m net decrease to Housing Strategy and Enabling; in-year capital programme £90.431m (approved £99.997m, adjusted down £9.566m)
findings.quote: Following a detailed review of the housing delivery programme, a net reduction of £16.950m has been made. This reflects revised cashflow forecasts while main contract arrangements are finalised.

findings.paper_title: Report - Q1 - Place Directorate budget report - LMB HAP
findings.headline: £2.724m Q1 revenue overspend managed through planned reserve drawdown of £5.085m
findings.detail: Place Directorate forecasts year-end revenue overspend of £2.724m after drawing down £5.085m from reserves. While reserves are within MTFP and no additional drawdown is flagged, the underlying overspend before reserves is £7.809m, reflecting significant budget pressure. Reserves are being consumed to maintain budget.
findings.matters: The council is drawing planned reserves to manage an overspend at Q1, consuming resources intended for flexibility or future priorities.
findings.figures: £2.724m overspend after £5.085m reserve drawdown; £7.809m underlying overspend before reserves
findings.quote: The forecast outturn expenditure at Quarter 1 is an overspend of £2.724m which includes an approved use of earmarked reserves of £5.085m.

findings.paper_title: Report - Q1 - Place Directorate budget report - LMB HAP
findings.headline: Leisure services £0.900m overspend driving Cabinet-level escalation for Salford Community Leisure
findings.detail: Leisure Services forecasts £0.900m overspend from 'ongoing financial support for Salford Community Leisure (SCL).' The paper states 'A Cabinet report is being prepared for August 2026', indicating this is a known structural issue escalated for senior decision-making and future strategy.
findings.matters: An arm's length body requires material ongoing financial support and has been escalated to Cabinet, signalling either strategic uncertainty or structural deficits requiring policy decisions.
findings.figures: £0.900m overspend in Leisure services attributed to Salford Community Leisure
findings.quote: Leisure Services is currently forecasting a £0.900m overspend driven by ongoing financial support for Salford Community Leisure (SCL). A Cabinet report is being prepared for August 2026.

findings.paper_title: Report - Q1 - Place Directorate budget report - LMB HAP
findings.headline: Commercial properties portfolio generating £3.017m shortfall covered by reserve drawdown
findings.detail: The commercial portfolio forecasts a £3.017m shortfall against budget at Q1, managed through the Incentive Reserve established to support the commercial operating model. The paper notes the drawdown 'aligns with the reserve's intended purpose', but the magnitude of shortfall at Q1 indicates material underperformance against commercial strategy assumptions.
findings.matters: Commercial assets are underperforming budget expectations and requiring planned reserve use, raising questions about the soundness of commercial strategy assumptions.
findings.figures: £3.017m shortfall in commercial properties covered by Incentive Reserve
findings.quote: A forecast shortfall within the commercial portfolio is being proactively managed through the approved use of the Incentive Reserve. This reserve was established to support the Council's commercial operating model through market fluctuations. The proposed drawdown of £3.017m aligns with the reserve's intended purpose.

findings.paper_title: Report - Q1 - Place Directorate budget report - LMB HAP
findings.headline: Housing service forecasts £3.583m overspend and cannot deliver £1.000m planned savings target
findings.detail: Housing transferred to Place Directorate mid-year and is experiencing leadership transition. It forecasts £3.583m overspend from Housing Benefit Subsidy Loss and demand pressures in Supported Housing and Housing Options. The budgeted £1.000m savings target is undeliverable: the service states it is 'not yet sufficiently embedded within the directorate to identify, develop and deliver sustainable savings of this scale without risking service performance' and will require 'further work' to develop a plan once new leadership is in place.
findings.matters: A material £18.7m service recently reorganized cannot deliver budgeted savings and is consuming reserves, requiring future transformation work of uncertain outcome.
findings.figures: £3.583m overspend, £1.759m reserve draw, net £1.824m overspend after reserves; £1.000m savings target at risk
findings.quote: the service is not yet sufficiently embedded within the directorate to identify, develop and deliver sustainable savings of this scale without risking service performance. It is therefore anticipated that further work will be required once the new leadership arrangements are in place to develop a robust and deliverable savings plan.
